prompt: Which food allergens require mandatory labeling in the UK but not in the US, Canada, and Australia?
answer:
**Celery is the only one of the UK’s 14 mandatory allergen categories that is not generally a mandatory allergen declaration category in the US, Canada, or Australia.**

For clarity:

| UK allergen not included in the US major-allergen list | Status in Canada/Australia |
|---|---|
| Celery | Generally not a mandatory priority-allergen category in either country |
| Mustard | Mandatory in Canada, but not a US major allergen |
| Lupin | Mandatory in Australia, but not a US major allergen |
| Molluscs | Mandatory in Canada, though not a US major allergen; generally not a separate mandatory category in Australia |
| Sulphur dioxide/sulphites | Also subject to mandatory declaration thresholds in Canada and Australia, although not a US FALCPA major allergen |

The US has nine major allergens, while the UK has 14. The comparison must also account for terminology: the UK requires declaration of **cereals containing gluten**, whereas the US specifically designates **wheat** as a major allergen. Sulphites may still require declaration in the US when present at regulated levels, even though they are not one of the US “major allergens.”
